data.narrative:
NordSpace is a Series A–stage space and aerospace company founded by Rahul Goel that has raised $38M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private-stage peers in the space sector, including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Of three valuation methods examined, only stage-progression analysis proved applicable. The method uses the $38M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression, yielding an implied valuation of $76M. Peer-median triangulation was not executable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within narrow filters (0 same-stage, 2 adjacent-stage peers identified); a broader sector median would introduce unjustified noise. Public-comparable anchoring via price-to-sales multiples could not proceed absent disclosed revenue for the target.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $65M to $87M, centered on $76M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single method and should be treated as provisional. Key uncertainties include NordSpace's revenue or near-term revenue trajectory (which would unlock public-comp anchoring), the trajectory and pace of capital deployment post-Series A, and relative competitive positioning versus the fragmented peer set. Further data on operational metrics would strengthen conviction in any point estimate within this band.
